# Interactive Visualization for Communication

Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience

People remember 10% of what they read, 20% of what they hear, 30% of what they see, 50% of what they see and hear, 70% of what they say and write, 90% of what they do. Engagment with information has been shown to improve the ability to retain information

- Interactive Plots (plotly)
- Interactive Maps (plotly, Leaflet)
- Interactive Tables (DT)
- Dashboards (flexdashboard)
- Interactive applications (shiny)
- Websites (Quarto, R Markdown, blogdown, Hugo, Jeckyll)

Interactivity allows users to engage with data in a way static visuals cannot: identify, isolate, visualize, zoom, highlight, filter, animate, change parameters

Interactive Visualization helps with both exploration and communication 

Import-> Tidy -> Transform/Visualize/Model -> Communicate

Aids exploratory data analysis by:
1. Investigating faster, identifying relationships or structure that would go missing, understand problems with data, models, or algorithms. 
2. Automating and efficiently sharing multiple dimensions of data/models/findings or complex analysis tasks
3. Helps users better undersantd and make decisions on data/models/findings
4. Tell a interesting or engaging story, presenting multple viewpoints
5. Allows users to focus on the aspects most important to them, making it more likely to understand, learn from, remember, and appreciate the data

# Plotly

Create and share interactive graphs
You can create a plotly object in two ways:
1. Transform a ggplot2 object into a plotly object (ggplotly())
2. Intialize a plotly object with plot_ly()/plot_geo()/plot_mapbox()

## ggplotly()
```{r}
p <- ggplot(*) + geom_*()
ggplotly(p)
```
Creates a graph and assigns it to a variable

```{r}
library(plotly)
```

## Example 1: New York Times Covid-19 Data

```{r}
# import data

cv_states <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/master/us-states.csv")

# format the date
cv_states$date <- as.Date(cv_states$date, format="%Y-%m-%d")

# create most recent day data frame
cv_states_today <- subset(cv_states, date==max(cv_states$date))

# inspect the data
str(cv_states)
dim(cv_states)
summary(cv_states)

# Scatterplot
cv_states_today |> 
           plot_ly(x = ~cases, y = ~deaths, 
                   type = 'scatter',
                   mode = 'markers',
                   color = ~state,
                   colors = "Blues")
```

```{r}
cv_states_today |> 
           plot_ly(x = ~cases, y = ~deaths, 
                   type = 'scatter',
                   mode = 'markers',
                   color = ~state,
                   sizes = c(5, 70),
                   marker = list(sizemode='diameter', opacity=0.5))
```

```{r}
cv_states_today |> 
  plot_ly(x = ~cases, y = ~deaths, 
          type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers', color = ~state,
          size = ~fips, sizes = c(5, 70), marker = list(sizemode='diameter', opacity=0.5),
          hoverinfo = 'text',
          text = ~paste( paste(state, ":", sep=""),
                         paste(" Cases per 100k: ", cases, sep="") ,
                         paste(" Deaths per 100k: ", deaths, sep=""),
                         paste(" CFR (%): ", fips,sep=""),
                         sep = "<br>")) 
```

```{r}
cv_states_today |> 
  plot_ly(x = ~cases, y = ~deaths, z = ~state,
          type = 'scatter3d', mode = 'markers', color = ~state,
          size = ~fips, sizes = c(5, 70), marker = list(sizemode='diameter', opacity=0.5),
          hoverinfo = 'text',
          text = ~paste( paste(state, ":", sep=""), 
                    paste(" Cases per 100k: ", cases, sep="") ,
              paste(" Deaths per 100k: ", deaths, sep=""),
              paste(" CFR (%): ", deaths,sep=""), 
              sep = "<br>")) |> 
  layout(title = "Cases, Deaths, and Naive Case Fatality Rate for US States",
          yaxis = list(title = "Cases"), 
          xaxis = list(title = "Deaths"),
         hovermode = "compare")
```

Hover Information
can specify what info will appear when hovering using hoverinfo through the text argument

Layout
specify chart labels through layout()
hovermode = "compare" allows comparing multiple points

3D Scatterplot
Can add a 3rd dimension using type = 'scatter3d', define the dimension as z

## Scatterplot with ggplotly()

Create a scatterplot with ggplotly() with 1 additional line of code --> allows taking advantage of geom_smooth

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(cv_states_today, aes(x=cases, y=deaths, size=fips)) + 
          geom_point() + geom_smooth()
ggplotly(p)
```

Add annotations to the plot
```{r}
p <- ggplot(cv_states_today, aes(x=cases, y=deaths, size=fips)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth() +
  annotate("text", 
           x = max(cv_states_today$cases),
           y = max(cv_states_today$deaths),
           label = paste('Cor =', cor(cv_states_today$cases, cv_states_today$deaths)))
fig <- ggplotly(p)
```

Line Graph
```{r}
cv_states |> 
plot_ly(x = ~date, y = ~deaths, color = ~state, type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
        hoverinfo = 'text',
        text = ~paste(paste(state, ":", sep=""), 
                  paste("Date: ", date, sep=""),
                  paste(" Deaths (total): ", deaths, sep=""), 
                  paste(" Deaths per 100k: ",  deaths, sep=""), sep = "<br>"))
```

Line Graph: ggplotly()
```{r}
g1 = plot_ly(cv_states, x = ~date, y = ~deaths, color = ~state, type = "scatter", mode = "lines")
g2 = ggplot(cv_states, aes(x = date, y = cases, color = state)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = .5, alpha = 0.5)
g2_plotly <- ggplotly(g2)
subplot(g1, g2_plotly)
```

Specifying text with ggplotly()
```{r}
g1 = ggplot(cv_states, aes(x = date, y = cases, color = state, 
              text=paste(paste(state, ":", sep=""), 
                         paste("Date: ", date, sep=""),
                    paste(" Cases (total): ", cases, sep=""),
                      sep = "<br>") )) + 
          geom_line() + geom_point(size = .5, alpha = 0.5) 
ggplotly(g1, tooltip = "text")
```

Histograms
```{r}
g1 <- cv_states_today |> 
  plot_ly(x = ~deaths, type = "histogram", xbins = list(size = 1, end=30 ))
g2 <- cv_states_today |> ggplot( aes(x=deaths)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=1)
g2_plotly <- ggplotly(g2)
subplot(g1, g2_plotly)
```

Heatmap
Useful for displaying three dimensional data in two dimensions, using color for the third dimension

```{r}
library(tidyr)
cv_states_mat <- cv_states |> 
            select(state, date, deaths) |> 
            filter(date>"2020-03-31") |> 
            filter(deaths < 10)
cv_states_mat2 <- as.data.frame(pivot_wider(cv_states_mat,
                                            names_from = state,
                                            values_from = deaths))
rownames(cv_states_mat2) <- cv_states_mat2$date
cv_states_mat2$date <- NULL
head(cv_states_mat2)

data <- as.matrix(cv_states_mat2)

plot_ly(x=colnames(data), y=rownames(data),
             z=~data,
             type="heatmap",
             showscale=T)

# 3D Surface using type = "surface"
plot_ly(x=colnames(cv_states_mat2), y=rownames(cv_states_mat2),
             z=~cv_states_mat2,
             type="surface",
             showscale=F)
```

Choropleth Maps
Illustrate data across geographic ares by shading regions with different colors

```{r}
library(dplyr)
cv_CFR <- cv_states_today |> select(state, fips) # select data

# Get state abbreviations and map to state names
st_crosswalk <- tibble(state = state.name) |>
   bind_cols(tibble(abb = state.abb)) |> 
   bind_rows(tibble(state = "District of Columbia", abb = "DC"))
cv_CFR2 <- left_join(cv_CFR, st_crosswalk, by = "state")
cv_CFR2$state.name <- cv_CFR2$state
cv_CFR2$state <- cv_CFR2$abb
cv_CFR2$abb <- NULL

# Create hover text
cv_CFR2$hover <- with(cv_CFR, paste(state.name, '<br>', "CFR:", fips))

# Set up mapping details
set_map_details <- list(
  scope = 'usa',
  projection = list(type = 'albers usa'),
  showlakes = TRUE,
  lakecolor = toRGB('white')
)

# Create the map
fig <- plot_geo(cv_CFR2, locationmode = 'USA-states') |> 
  add_trace(
    z = ~fips, 
    text = ~hover, 
    locations = ~state,
    color = ~fips, 
    colors = 'Blues'
  )
fig <- fig |> colorbar(title = "CFR")
fig <- fig |> layout(
    title = paste('CFR by State as of', Sys.Date(), '<br>(Hover for value)'),
    geo = set_map_details
  )
fig
```

# Interactive Tables
```{r}
library(DT)
cv_california <- cv_states |> filter(state=="California") |> select(date,cases,deaths,fips)
datatable(cv_california)
```
